clue.text: Enter Gordon: nearly all tremble in the Southeast

indicators.note: to tremble is to shake, so the letters of the fodder are shaken into a new order
nearly says the word all loses its last letter

parts.note: all, taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A man called Gordon is told to come in while the whole of the south-east of England shakes.
explanation.walkthrough: ENGLAND and GARDEN tempt from the fodder, but 'nearly all' adds AL, which 'tremble' mixes in too. Greater London is the administrative region around the capital in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital's metropolitan county is the largest urban area in the south-eastern corner of England, so it stands for that region here.

clue.text: Dubiously legal, if extraordinary, performance

definitions.meaning: extraordinary ... is the questionable transfer of suspects to other countries for interrogation
a performance of a song or piece of music

explanation.surface: A remarkable show that may not be quite within the law.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rendering of music or drama and, in the phrase extraordinary rendition, a legally dubious handover of prisoners.

clue.text: Passage from Kama Sutra is lewd

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A section of the famous Indian sex manual is judged indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Sutra is lewd': sutrA IS LEwd.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway between rows of seats is a passage people walk along.

clue.text: Animal's spirit finally departed

parts.note: elan is dash or spirit

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of departed

explanation.surface: An animal's life force has at last left it.
explanation.definitionFit: An African antelope is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Butcher's boy, once a president's double

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang a butcher's hook is a look
Al is a boy's name
Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, a former US president

explanation.surface: A butcher's lad turns out to be the spitting image of a former president.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's for LOOK is Cockney rhyming slang, a British usage: butcher's hook = look.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who closely resembles another is that person's double.

clue.text: Nationalist liberating society from squalor and poverty

indicators.note: liberating ... from says one letter is set free and another put in its place

parts.note: seediness is squalor or shabbiness

explanation.surface: A nationalist movement promises to free society from squalor and want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberating society from' swaps the first S of SEEDINESS for N; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in want, lacking the basics of life, is the state of poverty.

clue.text: Town reportedly excluded a former dictator

parts.note: Hastings is a town on the Sussex coast

indicators.note: reportedly says the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: banned means excluded

explanation.surface: A town is said to have barred someone who once ruled as a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings is an English seaside town; BANNED said aloud sounds like BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings Banda ruled Malawi as president for life until 1994, an autocratic former leader.

clue.text: Young relative seeing old king and the changing of the guard

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
taken as written

indicators.note: changing of signals that the letters of the following words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A child watches the ceremony at the palace with an elderly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing of' turns THE GUARD into DAUGHTER, nodding to the Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of one's son or daughter is a young member of the family.

clue.text: Mixing up names is initially a symptom of this

definitions.text: Mixing up names is initially a symptom of this

indicators.note: mixing up says the letters are jumbled together
initially takes the opening letter of is

explanation.surface: Getting people's names confused is an early sign of a memory disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: NAMES and the I of 'is' are mixed up to AMNESI, then A; the whole clue also describes the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory would naturally cause someone to muddle names.

clue.text: Outside broadcast following golf tournament

indicators.note: following says the broadcast word comes after the tournament

parts.note: the Open is golf's championship
to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Television coverage comes after the big golf event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcast' looks like one phrase, but 'Outside' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done outside, not under a roof, is done in the open air.

clue.text: Inert compound, which is made up of three parts

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about an unreactive substance with three components.
explanation.definitionFit: Trine is an old word for threefold, consisting of three.

clue.text: Botham's in pursuit of cricketer, one who comes from southern India

definitions.text: one who comes from southern India

indicators.note: in pursuit of puts Ian behind the cricketer

parts.note: Rahul Dravid was an Indian Test batsman
Ian Botham was an England cricketer; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: England's Botham chases an Indian cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham was a famous English all-rounder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dravidian peoples, speakers of Tamil and related languages, live chiefly in the south of the subcontinent.

clue.text: Diana metamorphosed into a nymph

indicators.note: metamorphosed means transformed, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A myth in which the goddess Diana is changed into a water spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph of springs and rivers is the kind of spirit meant.

clue.text: Modelled or acted to a degree

indicators.note: modelled means shaped, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone posed or performed to a certain extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a degree' reads as 'somewhat', but 'to' is fodder and 'a degree' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A PhD is the highest university qualification, a type of academic award.

clue.text: Turned and sniffed as son finally left for a week

indicators.note: left for says one letter leaves and another takes its place

parts.note: snivelled means sniffed tearfully

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of son

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: Someone turned round and sniffled as their son went away for seven days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son finally' is N; 'left for a week' swaps that N in SNIVELLED for W.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to turn round on a pivot.

clue.text: Oscar left US city as penance, perhaps

indicators.note: left says the letter departs from the city's name

parts.note: Sacramento is the capital of California
Oscar is O in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar quit an American city to atone for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is one of the rites of the Catholic Church, an example of a sacred ritual.

clue.text: It's most imprudent in America, however

definitions.meaning: read as two words, it means the least sensible
an American word meaning at any rate or anyway

explanation.surface: Americans think it is very foolish, nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage the word means at least or anyway, and split it means the opposite of most sensible.

clue.text: Imagine, perhaps, having an age to compose a musical opus

parts.note: Imagine is a John Lennon song, an example
a cycle is an age or aeon

explanation.surface: Writing the Lennon piece took so long it might as well be a big composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' joins the pieces and 'to compose' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A song cycle is a set of songs composed as one work, a musical opus.

clue.text: Rampaging fauns causing chaos

indicators.note: rampaging creatures run wild, so the letters run wild

explanation.surface: Wild goat-men run riot in a woodland scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An army acronym for a total mess, it means a state of confusion.

clue.text: First bit of advice's free — no charge for the roads

indicators.note: first bit of takes the opening letter of advice
free signals letters released into a new order

explanation.surface: A tip that costs nothing: no fee for using the highways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' turns NO CHARGE into NCHORAGE. 'Roads' is the nautical word for a sheltered stretch where ships anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadstead, or roads, is a place where ships may anchor offshore.

clue.text: Letters found in Secretary of State's apartment

indicators.note: only some letters of the name are found, the opening ones

parts.note: Condoleezza Rice was US Secretary of State

explanation.surface: Documents discovered in a senior minister's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Condoleezza Rice was US Secretary of State 2005-09; the start of her first name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A condominium unit, a condo, is the American word for an owned flat.

clue.text: Raged about poor Tom

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters go round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stormed around at a pitiful man.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Edgar disguises himself as the madman Poor Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's character takes the guise of a beggar called Poor Tom.

clue.text: Keep an eye on dog?

definitions.meaning: to dog someone is to follow and observe them

explanation.surface: Should one keep an eye on the dog?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to observe and to shadow, as one dogs a suspect.

clue.text: Diamonds found beneath raised area in part of Kent

indicators.note: in a down answer, beneath puts this letter after the weal

parts.note: a weal is a raised mark on the skin
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in cards

explanation.surface: Gems discovered under a hill in the Kent countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is a wooded area of Kent and Sussex in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weald is a region covering a large stretch of Kent.

clue.text: Bats tend to eat nuts with teeth

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
nuts means crazy, so these letters too are scrambled

explanation.surface: Bats are often seen eating nuts, using their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' turns TEND into DENT and 'nuts' turns EAT into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentate is a botanical and zoological word for toothed.

clue.text: Hard rock echoing in street in Argentina

indicators.note: echoing says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Heavy metal music reverberates along a road in Buenos Aires.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters stREET IN ARGentina, read backwards, give the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard igneous rock.

clue.text: Bruce, perhaps, meets joiners who used to write poetry

parts.note: Robert the Bruce was King of Scots, an example of a Robert
bridges join things together

explanation.surface: A Scotsman meets carpenters who were once poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meets' joins the pieces. Robert Bridges was Poet Laureate 1913-30.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges was an English poet, so he is one who used to write verse.
